newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares fall again in minimal deals.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares fall again in minimal deals.

text.p: Jordanian stocks dropped 0.51 percent on Monday in minimal buying compounded by a poor performance in the parallel market for newly established firms, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index dropped 0.78 points to 151.03 points in low turnover of 371,697 dinars ($524,995).
Deals in Livestock and Poultry, the day's busiest traded stock on the official market, totalled just 22,389 dinars, reflecting the scarcity of business.
But it was NAMICO, a diversified manufacturer of engineering products, that set the downward trend in trading on the parallel market, which trades before the opening of the official market.

NAMICO shares, which have nearly doubled in value during a recent surge to a high of 0.71 dinars last week, fell 0.04 dinars on Monday to 0.66 dinars in 122,000 dinars' worth of trade after an early speculative flurry petered out.
It nevertheless still accounted for the bulk of the day's turnover worth 145,551 dinars on the parallel market.
"The speculative trade on NAMICO has sharply dropped and this also affected the official market, already hurt by a shortage of cash," said Ibrahim Odeh of Wataniyeh Financial Services.
Overall falling shares in the official market outnumbered gainers by 27 to 10, with another nine trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.32 points to 80.16 points, 3.88 percent down from the start of the year.
